notes: Scaled, synthetic reproduction. The gym's experiments are finite preference-learning problems with hidden ground truth (see scoring/EXPERIMENTS.md). The paper's LLM numbers (Mistral-7B, HH-RLHF/UltraFeedback, GSM8K/MATH, MMLU/TruthfulQA) are not on this scale; they are kept unchanged under each experiment's `_paper_reported` key. `results` holds the gym's reference runs on the hidden test slice (scripts/reproduce.sh then scripts/evaluate_test.sh; training and evaluation are deterministic). Metrics with coefficient 0 are reported constraints enforced by a task gate, not ranked.

two_outcome_mode_collapse.description: Two-outcome social-choice prompts (paper Sec. 3, Prop. 3.1/3.2): a population prefers one of two completions with probability p in [0.55, 0.95]; the learner sees 8-40 sampled pairwise comparisons and a fixed non-uniform reference policy per prompt and must represent the population split. 300 visible train prompts (+ the paper's exact 80/20 example), 300 hidden test prompts.
two_outcome_mode_collapse.notes: Scaled from the paper's single analytic 80/20 example to many prompts with finite, noisy comparisons; scored only on hidden-test prompts whose population preference lives in eval/test/. Task gate: the population-majority completion must remain the most probable one on >= 75% of prompts.

preference_kl.description: Mean KL(population preference || learned policy) over test prompts (per-prompt cap 20 nats). Penalises both majority collapse and over-flattening.

minority_log_ratio_error.description: Mean |log(policy minority probability / population minority share)| (per-prompt cap 30): how many e-folds the minority view is under- or over-represented (paper Prop. 3.1 quantity).

_paper_reported.source: Paper Sec. 3.1 / Prop. 3.1-3.2, 80% vs 20% example with beta = 0.1 (analytic; uniform reference)
_paper_reported.gym_check: The visible train context `two_outcome_paper_80_20` reproduces this example; eval/train/evaluate.py reports it under diagnostics (paper_80_20_minority_probability, paper_80_20_majority_overweight).

sequence_diversity_best_of_n.description: Sequence-level preference learning (paper Sec. 4.1-4.2): 7-token sequences over a 21-token vocabulary (about 1.8e9 sequences; ~16 tokens per position are rarely-produced incoherent tokens). Per prompt the learner sees a fixed reference chain policy and 2000 Bradley-Terry comparisons between reference samples, and outputs a full chain policy. Scored on 32 hidden-test prompts against the hidden population distribution, hidden verifier sets for hard best-of-N problems, and hidden token-coherence labels.
sequence_diversity_best_of_n.notes: Synthetic stand-in for LLM generation: the output space cannot be enumerated, token-level temperature and sequence-level (global) temperature differ, and incoherent tokens play the role of non-word tokens. Task gate: expected population reward of the policy must not fall below that of the fixed reference policy.

best_of_128_success_hard.description: Mean probability that 128 independent samples contain a verified solution, over 6 hard problems per prompt (solutions are coherent sequences matching a hidden 4-position pattern, away from the population mode, with population mass 0.2-2%). Computed exactly from the policy.

population_kl.description: Exact sequence-level KL(population distribution || policy) (per-prompt cap 60 nats): proportional representation of the population over whole sequences.

coherence.description: Probability that a sampled sequence contains no incoherent token (the paper's lexical-integrity / non-word statistic).

_paper_reported.source: Paper Table 1, hard splits, best-of-128 accuracy (Mistral-7B, UltraFeedback)
_paper_reported.diversity_quality: Fig. 1-2: SPL Pareto-dominates DPO with token-level temperature on diversity vs quality; token temperature above ~1.5 yields mostly non-word tokens (no single table value).

calibration_multiple_choice.description: Four-option multiple-choice prompts (paper Sec. 4.3): each prompt has a hidden distribution over which option is correct; the learner sees 20-80 sampled pairwise comparisons and a fixed reference answer distribution, and outputs answer probabilities. 600 visible train prompts, 600 hidden test prompts. Metrics are expectations over the hidden correct answer.
calibration_multiple_choice.notes: Synthetic substitute for MMLU/TruthfulQA logit calibration; correct options are placed at random positions. Task gate (evaluator-owned): expected accuracy must be at least the accuracy of picking the option with the best (wins - losses) comparison count, minus 0.01 (test floor 0.4717; DPO-level accuracy, the paper's 'without sacrificing accuracy' constraint). Hardening (iteration 11): accuracy coefficient 0.5 -> 0 (gate-enforced constraint), Brier 0.75 -> 1.0 and primary, ECE 1.0 -> 0.5; see HARDENING.md.

brier_score.description: Expected multi-class Brier score against the hidden correct answer (a proper scoring rule: rewards both calibration and putting mass on the right option). Primary calibration metric of the rank.

expected_calibration_error.description: 10-bin ECE of top-answer confidence against expected top-answer accuracy (the paper's headline calibration statistic). Weighted below Brier because ECE alone is minimised by uninformative constant-confidence answers.

accuracy.description: Expected accuracy of the most probable answer (ties broken toward the lowest option index). Constraint, enforced by the task gate (accuracy >= comparison-vote accuracy - 0.01); reported but not ranked, because honest methods differ here only by a few near-tie argmax flips, which normalisation by the cohort spread would amplify into noise.

_paper_reported.source: Paper Sec. 4.3 / Fig. 4 (MMLU, TruthfulQA; values reported only in figures)
_paper_reported.claim: DPO (global temperature 1) is less calibrated than the SFT base; increasing SPL global temperature lowers ECE and Brier below the base model while keeping accuracy similar.
